page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.3xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via KVM. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 22 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Local storage is not bundled, requiring external block storage for persistent disk needs. The instance includes a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and features instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multithreaded capacity alongside modest single-threaded throughput. Under stress-ng, single-core processing scores 1354.88, while multithreaded execution achieves 10809.26. Geekbench testing records a single-core score of 1087.0 and a multi-core score of 5444.0, with solid parallel task handling represented by a Clang compilation score of 9645.0 and ray tracing at 8984.0. Large-block memory throughput reaches 55.98 GB/sec for reads and 38.69 GB/sec for writes, supporting 10.54 million Redis SET operations per second. However, memory-focused PassMark testing ranks lower at 1762.79, and static web serving throughput measures 6.31 GB/sec.

The 1:2 RAM-to-CPU ratio and dedicated core model position ecs.hfc5.3xlarge as an efficient compute-oriented configuration where parallel processing requirements exceed memory footprint needs. Hardware tradeoffs include the total absence of local NVMe storage, modest baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and legacy single-thread performance relative to modern CPU architectures. The instance does not bundle GPU acceleration, limiting large machine learning tasks; small 135M parameter LLM inference handles 115.28 text generation tokens per second, but 7B models drop to 6.84 tokens per second. Consequently, this server is suitable for batch compute jobs, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, microservices, and compute-focused backend processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.3xlarge is a compute-focused instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores and 24.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local disk storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and presenting a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, multi-core metrics perform within the median range, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 11911.02, a Geekbench multi-core result of 5444.0, and Clang compilation scores of 9645.0, whereas single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles. With 10.54 million Redis SET operations per second and instruction set support including AVX-512F, this instance delivers efficient parallel processing for multi-threaded build systems, CI/CD pipelines, distributed batch jobs, and compute-intensive microservice workloads.
